answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited reputation system tied to costly, time-locked deposits: an agent must lock tokens before it can submit work, and its deposit is slashed if independent reviewers verify fraud. New identities start with little influence, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply voting power; each account needs its own capital and waiting period. An attacker must therefore buy and immobilize funds, then risk losing them. The ledger can label deposits timber, ivory, and pearl without treating those labels as proof of identity.
